basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 1-14.' and it opens 'VERS. 1-14.-- Dixitque Dominus ad Abram: Ecce testamentum meum tecum, et eris pater'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 1-14.-- Dixitque Dominus ad Abram: Ecce testamentum meum tecum, et eris pater multitudinis gentium, et non vocabitur nomen tuum Abram, sed erit nomen tuum Abraham, quia patrem multarum gentium posui te. Dicunt autem Hebraei quod ex nomine suo Deus, quod apud illos tetragrammum est, id est: Jot, et he, vau, e litteram Abrae et Sarae addiderat. Dicebatur enim primum Abram, quod interpretatur pater excelsus, et postea vocatus est Abraham, pater multarum; nam quod gentium non habetur, | in nomine subauditur. Nec mirandum quare, cum apud Graecos et quosdam a littera videatur addita, nos e litteram Hebraeam additam dixerimus. Idioma enim linguae est per e quidem scribere, sed per a legere; sicut e contra per a scribere et per e legere.
